balanced.summary: A sensible start for one person chatting: an 8k context and a model that stays loaded for half an hour.
balanced.details: It fixes the context at 8192 tokens, so memory use is modest and predictable even on a large GPU, and keeps a model in memory for 30 minutes after its last request so follow-up questions answer quickly.
balanced.when_to_change: Start here for chat. Move to long-context for big documents, or to low-memory when the GPU is shared.
balanced.risks: A prompt longer than 8192 tokens is cut off. The model's memory stays reserved for half an hour.
balanced.example: A chat that fits in about 12 pages of text.

big-model-spread.summary: For one big model: it is always spread across every GPU, with a 16k context.
big-model-spread.details: A model too large for one card needs several. Spreading is forced, so every loaded model is divided across all GPUs.
big-model-spread.when_to_change: Use it for a model that does not fit on a single GPU.
big-model-spread.risks: Without NVLink the cards talk over PCIe, which is slower than a model that fits on one card.

long-context.summary: For long documents: a 128k context with an 8-bit conversation cache and flash attention.
long-context.details: A 131072-token context holds a book-length document. Storing the conversation memory in 8-bit numbers roughly halves its size, and flash attention keeps the working memory small.
long-context.when_to_change: Use it to summarize or question long documents.
long-context.risks: Even with 8-bit storage the cache for a large model can use tens of GB. Answers may slow as the document grows.

low-latency.summary: For the fastest first answer: one request at a time, an 8k context, flash attention and a model that never unloads.
low-latency.details: Keeping the model loaded forever removes the load delay, and a single request at a time gives each answer the whole GPU.
low-latency.when_to_change: Use it for a personal assistant or an editor plug-in that must respond immediately.
low-latency.risks: The model's memory is held until the server stops, so other engines cannot use it.
low-latency.example: A code assistant that answers within a second of your keystroke.

low-memory.summary: For a shared GPU: a 4k context, an 8-bit cache, one loaded model and quick unloading after a minute.
low-memory.details: It keeps memory use small and gives the memory back one minute after the last request, so other programs can use the GPU.
low-memory.when_to_change: Use it on a GPU that several engines or a desktop share.
low-memory.risks: Short context cuts long prompts, and the model reloads for each new burst of requests.
low-memory.example: A GPU that also runs a video editor.

many-models.summary: For switching between several models: up to three stay loaded per GPU and unload after ten idle minutes.
many-models.details: Keeping several models in memory makes switching between them instant, as long as they all fit.
many-models.when_to_change: Use it when you compare models or run different models for different tasks.
many-models.risks: Several models share the GPU memory, so large ones may be loaded only partly on the GPU.
many-models.example: Switching between a coding model and a chat model all day.

max-throughput.summary: For several users at once: four parallel requests per model, an 8k context each, and flash attention on.
max-throughput.details: Four requests are answered in parallel, so a group is served without waiting in line. The context memory is multiplied by four, so budget about 32768 tokens of conversation memory per loaded model.
max-throughput.when_to_change: Use it for a small team or a few agents sharing one model.
max-throughput.risks: More parallel requests use more memory and slow each answer a little. A model that barely fits may no longer fit.
max-throughput.example: Four colleagues asking questions at the same moment.
